subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: Purple and the Pacific War
description: One-minute skill: Purple and the Pacific War.

hook.text: American codebreakers cracked Japan's top diplomatic cipher — called 'Purple' — before Pearl Harbor.

buildup.text: William Friedman's team reverse-engineered Japan's cipher machine without ever seeing the physical device.

discovery.text: They built a replica from scratch using only intercepted messages. It matched perfectly.

twist.text: America could read Japan's diplomatic messages but still failed to prevent the Pearl Harbor attack.

climax.text: Breaking a code doesn't help if the intelligence isn't shared or acted on in time.

punchline.text: The code was broken. The warning was missed.

quiz.question: What was unique about how American codebreakers cracked the Purple cipher?
options: They built a replica machine without ever seeing the original
They captured a Purple machine in battle
A Japanese defector provided the key
